function.mechanism: Hydrophilic polymer that increases viscosity and forms gels, improving water binding, texture, and dispersion stability.
common_food_categories: other food categories (category-specific limits in 21 CFR 184.1724)

adi.basis: No numerical ADI needed (EFSA re-evaluation conclusion).

efsa.key_finding: No safety concern at refined exposure for reported uses; insufficient data for certain infant/young-child FSMP categories.

fda.notes: Listed under 21 CFR Part 184 (direct food substances affirmed as GRAS) with category-specific maximum use levels and functional-use limits.

concerns.summary: At therapeutic pediatric doses used for reflux (about 417-834 mg/kg bw/day), gastrointestinal side effects have been reported, including rare intragastric mass formation.
EFSA noted possible hypersensitivity issues from protein impurities and recommended reducing protein limits in specifications as much as possible.
Data were considered insufficient for adequate safety assessment in infants/young children consuming specific foods for special medical purposes (FC 13.1.5.1 and 13.1.5.2).

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA and JECFA concluded no numerical ADI needed / ADI not specified for alginic acid and salts including E401.
EFSA found no genotoxicity concern for alginic acid and salts using available data and read-across.
EFSA did not identify carcinogenic concern in available long-term animal studies.
Recent clinical studies in reflux populations reported no major new safety signals for alginate-based oral products.

populations: infants/young children on special medical purpose diets
adi_exceedance.notes: Formal ADI exceedance is not applicable because ADI is not numerical; EFSA still recommends keeping infant/young-child exposure below therapeutic-dose ranges where GI side effects occur.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory consensus is favorable (EU authorized, US GRAS, JECFA ADI not specified) with no strong genotoxic/carcinogenic signal for typical use, but there are meaningful caveats for vulnerable infant FSMP populations and high-dose GI effects.
key_factors: EFSA 2017: no numerical ADI needed and no safety concern at refined exposure for reported uses.
FDA: sodium alginate listed under 21 CFR Part 184 with explicit use conditions (21 CFR 184.1724).
EFSA identified data gaps for specific infant/young-child FSMP categories.
No IARC listing found for sodium alginate in current IARC classifications dataset.
